programme.title: MOTD Live: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: USA v Australia (Kick-off 8.00pm). Gabby Logan presents coverage of the Group D match at Seattle Stadium in the USA. These nations have faced each other on four previous occasions, but this is the first competitive fixture between the two, with all others being friendlies. The most recent of those games took place in Colorado last October, and saw the Americans dominate possession and eventually triumph 2-1, bringing an end to a 12-match unbeaten run for the Socceroos, in what was also a first defeat for Tony Popovic as coach. Both teams impressed in their openers, with USA overcoming Paraguay 4-1, and the Aussies claiming a shock 2-0 victory over Türkiye. With analysis from Olivier Giroud, Wayne Rooney and Theo Walcott

programme.title: MOTD Live: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Ecuador v Curaçao (Kick-off 1.00am). Coverage of the Group E match at Kansas City Stadium in the USA. Both of these teams were exemplary in qualifying for this tournament, with Ecuador only suffering two losses in their 18 matches in the CONMEBOL region as they went on to finish second in the standings, while Curaçao were undefeated in all 10 of their matches across two stages in the CONCACAF region. The team known as The Blue Wave are now one of just five Caribbean teams to compete at a World Cup finals, and coming into this staging of the competition no team from the region had progressed beyond the group stage, with Cuba having made a quarter-final appearance in 1938 when the finals only consisted of a single-elimination tournament involving 16 teams. Both countries had disappointing results in their first games of the finals, as Ecuador conceded late on to lose 1-0 to Ivory Coast, while Curacao were thrashed 7-1 by Germany in their finals debut

programme.title: MOTD Live: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Netherlands v Sweden (Kick-off 6.00pm). Mark Chapman presents coverage of the Group F match at Houston Stadium in the USA. The Dutch secured their place at this World Cup by finishing top of their qualifying group ahead of Poland, Finland, Malta and Lithuania, winning six of their eight matches and drawing the other two, and scoring 27 goals in the process while conceding just four. However, they had a minor setback in their opener when they were held to a 2-2 draw by Japan. Sweden had to work much harder to qualify, eventually getting through via the play-offs, but they got off to an excellent start in these finals with an emphatic 5-1 victory over Tunisia. This is scheduled to be the 1,000th match to take place at a World Cup finals, and the seventh meeting overall between the two nations, who were also drawn in the same group in 2002 when Samurai Blue served as co-hosts alongside South Korea. Goals from Hiroaki Morishima and former Bolton Wanderers-loanee Hidetoshi Nakata inspired the Japanese to a 2-0 win on that occasion in Osaka and helped them top the table ahead of Belgium and Russia, while also condemning the Eagles of Carthage to fourth place and an early exit. Since that time there have been four more encounters between these nations, with Japan triumphing in three of those games, including a 2-0 friendly win most recently in 2023, while the North Africans claimed a 3-0 win in the final of the 2022 Kirin Cup, which is an occasional invitation event organised and staged by Japan

Sustainability is in the spotlight as pioneering growers reveal why cork could be a game-changing material - and how it's already transforming the way they garden. There's an ambitious show garden co-designed by Professor Alice Roberts, bringing the story of evolution to life through plants, and a first-time designer whose passion for railways has inspired a unique garden guaranteed to turn heads

Together, they feature secret laboratories and historic seedlings, topiary cats and exquisite portraits. Toby Jones narrates

Travelling across the UK, he has honest conversations with young men about how they are feeling and what is really going on in their lives, exploring in detail what is shaping the attitudes and outlook of this generation. His journey takes him to Middlesbrough, where he first made his name in management, to meet young men struggling with unemployment; to a secondary school in Essex, to discover how boys are coping with the demands of the current education system; and to a prison, where he speaks with young inmates to explore what really led them into crime

Daniel De Simone investigates and finds the shadowy figures behind the attacks were also behind fake far-right groups trying to stoke hatred and division in the UK. The fires fit a pattern in which hostile states such as Russia are increasingly using proxies here to do their dirty work. So could Russia be behind the Starmer fires?

Starting in Seoul, they uncover the crispy secrets of Korean Fried Chicken and reveal the key ingredient in Gochujang sauce. Continuing south to Icheon, they investigate a rice-based alcoholic spirit that outsells all others in Korea. In Cheonan they discover the reason for the massive popularity of pork luncheon meat - aka spam - and find out how it's made. A short detour to the beach at Dacheon leads to a surprising and unforgettable seafood with a nickname fit for the playground. Finally, in Gwangju, they enter a world of kimchi, and learn the key to its global expansion

programme.title: Heir Hunters

programme.title: The M Factor: Shredding the Silence on Menopause
programme.desc: Menopause is a silent epidemic that affects the health and wellbeing of millions of women. In addition to experiencing traumatic physical symptoms, women often struggle with related emotional stresses. Symptoms can derail careers, disrupt relationships and cause unnecessary physical suffering. programme.title: FIFA World Cup 26 Live
programme.desc: USA v Australia (Kick-off 8.00pm). Marie Crowe presents coverage of the Group D match at Seattle Stadium in the USA. These nations have faced each other on four previous occasions, but this is the first competitive fixture between the two, with all others being friendlies. The most recent of those games took place in Colorado last October, and saw the Americans dominate possession and eventually triumph 2-1, bringing an end to a 12-match unbeaten run for the Socceroos, in what was also a first defeat for Tony Popovic as coach. Both teams reached the knockout stage in Qatar four years ago but failed to make it further than the last-16, with the USA eliminated by the Netherlands following a 3-1 defeat, and Australia suffering a narrow 2-1 loss to eventual champions Argentina

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 26 Live
programme.desc: Scotland v Morocco (Kick-off 11.00pm). Marie Crowe presents coverage of the Group C match at Boston Stadium in the USA. This is the second World Cup meeting between these nations, with the previous one also being a group-stage match at France '98, the last time Scotland appeared at the finals. It was the Africans who came out on top with a comfortable 3-0 win in Saint-Étienne over a side that featured the likes of Jim Leighton, Colin Hendry, John Collins and Gordon Durie, and was managed by Craig Brown. Morocco will go into this contest as favourites to prevail once again after an impressive performance in their opener, which saw them draw 1-1 with Brazil. However, it is the Scots who sit on top of the table at this early stage following a 1-0 win against Haiti, which was their first victory in a World Cup finals since they defeated Sweden in 1990

programme.desc: The story of an entrepreneur whose identity was stolen and used for criminal activities online, leaving him facing messages from people accusing him of conning them out of tens of thousands of pounds. His attempt to find out more and get his online identity back takes him on an international journey and he discovers that it's not only those being conned who are the victims. programme.desc: Bringing extra entertainment to the 2026 FIFA World Cup, this vodcast is hosted by The Young Offenders stars Dominic MacHale and Shane Casey. With many matches kicking off overnight, the duo do the late-night watching so viewers don't have to, delivering their trademark Cork humour and chaos alongside a round-up of all the latest action and talking points from the tournament

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 26 Live
programme.desc: Netherlands v Sweden (Kick-off 6.00pm). Tony O'Donoghue presents coverage of the Group F match at Houston Stadium in the USA. The Dutch secured their place at this World Cup by finishing top of their qualifying group ahead of Poland, Finland, Malta and Lithuania, winning six of their eight matches and drawing the other two, and scoring 27 goals in the process while conceding just four. However, they had a minor setback in their opener when they were held to a 2-2 draw by Japan. Sweden had to work much harder to qualify, eventually getting through via the play-offs, but they got off to an excellent start in these finals with an emphatic 5-1 victory over Tunisia. With analysis from Didi Hamann

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 26 Live
programme.desc: Germany v Ivory Coast (Kick-off 9.00pm). Tony O'Donoghue presents coverage of the Group E match at Toronto Stadium in Canada. There has only been one previous encounter between these nations, a 2009 friendly match that ended in a 2-2 draw in Gelsenkirchen, and Les Éléphants will have to improve on their World Cup record against European opposition if they are to stand a chance of claiming a victory here. In four meetings against teams from Europe, they have a record of one win, one draw and two losses, with the sole win coming against Serbia and Montenegro at the 2006 tournament in Germany. While Die Mannschaft have a proud World Cup record overall they have failed to deliver since lifting the trophy in 2014, not even progressing beyond the group stage in both 2018 and 2022 after finishing fourth and third in the group standings respectively. Both sides got their campaigns underway with victories, as Germany thrashed Curacao 7-1 and Ivory Coast nicked a late 1-0 win against Ecuador. With analysis from Didi Hamann

programme.title: Frameworks 28
programme.desc: In the throes of his overstimulated, energy-poor midlife, a man fantasises about everything he'd love to do in retirement, once he finally has the 'time'. Comedy animation, with the voice of Domhnall Gleeson

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 26 Live
programme.desc: Ecuador v Curaçao (Kick-off 1.00am). Coverage of the Group E match at Kansas City Stadium in the USA. Both of these teams were exemplary in qualifying for this tournament, with Ecuador only suffering two losses in their 18 matches in the CONMEBOL region as they went on to finish second in the standings, while Curaçao were undefeated in all 10 of their matches across two stages in the CONCACAF region. The team known as The Blue Wave are now one of just five Caribbean teams to compete at a World Cup finals, and coming into this staging of the competition no team from the region had progressed beyond the group stage, with Cuba having made a quarter-final appearance in 1938 when the finals only consisted of a single-elimination tournament involving 16 teams. Both countries had disappointing results in their first games of the finals, as Ecuador conceded late on to lose 1-0 to Ivory Coast, while Curacao were thrashed 7-1 by Germany in their finals debut

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 26 Live
programme.desc: Mexico v South Korea (Kick-off 2.00am). Coverage of the Group A match at Guadalajara Stadium in Mexico. It's likely that the co-hosts will have a tougher challenge before them here, with Korea also on a high after picking up three points from their opener against Czechia, despite going a goal down in the second half

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 26 Live
programme.desc: USA v Australia (Kick-off 8.00pm). Marie Crowe presents coverage of the Group D match at Seattle Stadium in the USA. These nations have faced each other on four previous occasions, but this is the first competitive fixture between the two, with all others being friendlies. The most recent of those games took place in Colorado last October, and saw the Americans dominate possession and eventually triumph 2-1, bringing an end to a 12-match unbeaten run for the Socceroos, in what was also a first defeat for Tony Popovic as coach. Both teams reached the knockout stage in Qatar four years ago but failed to make it further than the last-16, with the USA eliminated by the Netherlands following a 3-1 defeat, and Australia suffering a narrow 2-1 loss to eventual champions Argentina

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 26 Live
programme.desc: Scotland v Morocco (Kick-off 11.00pm). Marie Crowe presents coverage of the Group C match at Boston Stadium in the USA. This is the second World Cup meeting between these nations, with the previous one also being a group-stage match at France '98, the last time Scotland appeared at the finals. It was the Africans who came out on top with a comfortable 3-0 win in Saint-Étienne over a side that featured the likes of Jim Leighton, Colin Hendry, John Collins and Gordon Durie, and was managed by Craig Brown. Morocco will go into this contest as favourites to prevail once again after an impressive performance in their opener, which saw them draw 1-1 with Brazil. However, it is the Scots who sit on top of the table at this early stage following a 1-0 win against Haiti, which was their first victory in a World Cup finals since they defeated Sweden in 1990

programme.title: Frameworks 28
programme.desc: In the throes of his overstimulated, energy-poor midlife, a man fantasises about everything he'd love to do in retirement, once he finally has the 'time'. Comedy animation, with the voice of Domhnall Gleeson

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 26 Live
programme.desc: Ecuador v Curaçao (Kick-off 1.00am). Coverage of the Group E match at Kansas City Stadium in the USA. Both of these teams were exemplary in qualifying for this tournament, with Ecuador only suffering two losses in their 18 matches in the CONMEBOL region as they went on to finish second in the standings, while Curaçao were undefeated in all 10 of their matches across two stages in the CONCACAF region. The team known as The Blue Wave are now one of just five Caribbean teams to compete at a World Cup finals, and coming into this staging of the competition no team from the region had progressed beyond the group stage, with Cuba having made a quarter-final appearance in 1938 when the finals only consisted of a single-elimination tournament involving 16 teams. Both countries had disappointing results in their first games of the finals, as Ecuador conceded late on to lose 1-0 to Ivory Coast, while Curacao were thrashed 7-1 by Germany in their finals debut

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 26 Live
programme.desc: Brazil v Haiti (Kick-off 1.30am). Coverage of the Group C match at Philadelphia Stadium in the USA. Brazil were second best for most of their opener against Morocco, but came away with a 1-1 draw, while Haiti performed admirably in a 1-0 defeat to Scotland. Brazil have registered large victories in the two previous encounters between these nations, claiming a 6-0 win in an international friendly in 2004, and more recently a 7-1 triumph in the group stage of the 2016 Copa America, which also took place in the United States, and saw then-Liverpool attacking midfielder Philippe Coutinho score a hat-trick. Despite a relatively poor record in qualifying the Seleção will have high hopes of performing well under the stewardship of former Real Madrid, Chelsea and AC Milan manager Carlo Ancelotti, who was appointed in May last year on a one-year contract, which has since been extended for another four years, and anything other than a victory in this match will be considered a catastrophe

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 26 Live
programme.desc: Türkiye v Paraguay (Kick-off 4.00am). Coverage of the Group D match at San Francisco Bay Area Stadium in Santa Clara, USA. Both sides need something from this fixture, with Türkiye abject in their 2-0 defeat to Australia, and Paraguay blown away by the USA in their opening contests. There has only been one previous meeting between these nations, a 0-0 draw in a 1995 friendly, but Paraguay will hope to emulate their results against European opposition in the group stage at their last World Cup appearance in South Africa in 2010, when they drew 1-1 against Italy and defeated Slovakia 2-0 on their way to finishing top of Group F. They subsequently overcame Japan in the last-16 via a penalty shootout, but then fell foul of a European nation in the quarter-finals, when they lost 1-0 to eventual champions Spain

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 26 Live
programme.desc: Netherlands v Sweden (Kick-off 6.00pm). Tony O'Donoghue presents coverage of the Group F match at Houston Stadium in the USA. The Dutch secured their place at this World Cup by finishing top of their qualifying group ahead of Poland, Finland, Malta and Lithuania, winning six of their eight matches and drawing the other two, and scoring 27 goals in the process while conceding just four. However, they had a minor setback in their opener when they were held to a 2-2 draw by Japan. Sweden had to work much harder to qualify, eventually getting through via the play-offs, but they got off to an excellent start in these finals with an emphatic 5-1 victory over Tunisia. With analysis from Didi Hamann

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 26 Live
programme.desc: Germany v Ivory Coast (Kick-off 9.00pm). Tony O'Donoghue presents coverage of the Group E match at Toronto Stadium in Canada. There has only been one previous encounter between these nations, a 2009 friendly match that ended in a 2-2 draw in Gelsenkirchen, and Les Éléphants will have to improve on their World Cup record against European opposition if they are to stand a chance of claiming a victory here. In four meetings against teams from Europe, they have a record of one win, one draw and two losses, with the sole win coming against Serbia and Montenegro at the 2006 tournament in Germany. While Die Mannschaft have a proud World Cup record overall they have failed to deliver since lifting the trophy in 2014, not even progressing beyond the group stage in both 2018 and 2022 after finishing fourth and third in the group standings respectively. Both sides got their campaigns underway with victories, as Germany thrashed Curacao 7-1 and Ivory Coast nicked a late 1-0 win against Ecuador. With analysis from Didi Hamann

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 26 Live
programme.desc: Tunisia v Japan (Kick-off 5.00am). Coverage of the Group F match at Monterrey Stadium in Mexico. Tunisia were thumped 5-1 by Sweden in their opener, while Japan played out an entertaining 2-2 against the Netherlands. This is scheduled to be the 1,000th match to take place at a World Cup finals, and the seventh meeting overall between the two nations, who were also drawn in the same group in 2002 when Samurai Blue served as co-hosts alongside South Korea. Goals from Hiroaki Morishima and former Bolton Wanderers-loanee Hidetoshi Nakata inspired the Japanese to a 2-0 win on that occasion in Osaka and helped them top the table ahead of Belgium and Russia, while also condemning the Eagles of Carthage to fourth place and an early exit. Since that time there have been four more encounters between these nations, with Japan triumphing in three of those games, including a 2-0 friendly win most recently in 2023, while the North Africans claimed a 3-0 win in the final of the 2022 Kirin Cup, which is an occasional invitation event organised and staged by Japan

programme.title: Rick Stein: From Venice to Istanbul
programme.desc: The chef continues his 900-mile road trip from Venice to Istanbul, sampling that array of gastronomic delights that lie on the route. In the penultimate episode Rick arrives in the Greek Peloponnese where he samples mouth-watering dishes such as rooster stew hilopites with mizithra cheese, and a home-made moussaka he claims is the best he have ever savoured. In his Symi island kitchen, Rick rolls up his sleeves to prepare galaktoboureko, a dessert of semolina custard in filo pastry, a favourite dish in Greece

programme.title: Rick Stein: From Venice to Istanbul
programme.desc: The chef's gastronomic road trip from Venice to Istanbul through the countries of the former Byzantine Empire is nearing its end as he leaves southern Greece for the shores of western Turkey. On the Cesme Peninsula Rick enjoys creamy Armola cheese matured in goat skins, Urla's famous red wine and the ultimate Turkish breakfast. He also cooks the country's iconic dish sultan's delight - a mouth-watering lamb stew on a bed of aubergine puree

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: The presenters hand over the reviewing reins to their mothers, who examine a range of small cars including the Renault Modus, Honda Jazz and Peugeot 1007. Comedian Omid Djalili is the Star in the Reasonably Priced Car

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson tests the agility of the Porsche Boxster S and Mercedes SLK as he drives them through a hail of Army snipers' bullets, plus a look at 1960s classics the Aston Martin DB5 and Jaguar E-type. Damon Hill is the Star in a Reasonably Priced Car

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul Whitehouse and Bob Mortimer head to Norfolk, where they attempt to ensnare a large pike - a fish that has eluded them on their trips so far. As they arrive and get their gear together, Bob introduces Paul to the surprisingly varied contents of his car boot, much to Paul's amusement. They gather their equipment and find a decent spot that should give them plenty of chances to catch and make camp for the day. They end their trip with a visit to a local pub, where Bob reveals a hidden trick

programme.title: Caribbean with Simon Reeve

programme.title: Rick Stein: From Venice to Istanbul
programme.desc: The chef continues his 900-mile road trip from Venice to Istanbul, sampling that array of gastronomic delights that lie on the route. In the penultimate episode Rick arrives in the Greek Peloponnese where he samples mouth-watering dishes such as rooster stew hilopites with mizithra cheese, and a home-made moussaka he claims is the best he have ever savoured. In his Symi island kitchen, Rick rolls up his sleeves to prepare galaktoboureko, a dessert of semolina custard in filo pastry, a favourite dish in Greece

programme.title: Rick Stein: From Venice to Istanbul
programme.desc: The chef's gastronomic road trip from Venice to Istanbul through the countries of the former Byzantine Empire is nearing its end as he leaves southern Greece for the shores of western Turkey. On the Cesme Peninsula Rick enjoys creamy Armola cheese matured in goat skins, Urla's famous red wine and the ultimate Turkish breakfast. He also cooks the country's iconic dish sultan's delight - a mouth-watering lamb stew on a bed of aubergine puree

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: The presenters hand over the reviewing reins to their mothers, who examine a range of small cars including the Renault Modus, Honda Jazz and Peugeot 1007. The Cadillac CTS-V is put to the test on the racetrack, Richard Hammond takes the BMW 3 Series for a spin, and the team discover how far a limousine can jump. Comedian Omid Djalili is the Star in the Reasonably Priced Car

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson tests the agility of the Porsche Boxster S and Mercedes SLK as he drives them through a hail of Army snipers' bullets, plus a look at 1960s classics the Aston Martin DB5 and Jaguar E-type. Damon Hill is the Star in a Reasonably Priced Car

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul Whitehouse and Bob Mortimer head to Norfolk, where they attempt to ensnare a large pike - a fish that has eluded them on their trips so far. As they arrive and get their gear together, Bob introduces Paul to the surprisingly varied contents of his car boot, much to Paul's amusement. They gather their equipment and find a decent spot that should give them plenty of chances to catch and make camp for the day. They end their trip with a visit to a local pub, where Bob reveals a hidden trick

programme.title: Caribbean with Simon Reeve
programme.desc: Simon meets the owner of a traditional wooden house in Barbados who has turned down millions of dollars from luxury property developers, then encounters marijuana growers on the volcanic island of St Vincent hoping that the drug will soon be decriminalised. On the South American mainland, Simon examines the mismanagement of Venezuela's natural resources, before crossing into Colombia, where he spends time with the Kogi - an indigenous people who have maintained their traditional forest lifestyle

programme.title: The Hairy Bikers' Chicken and Egg
programme.desc: Dave and Si cook chicken tagine with preserved lemons and olives for some rebel Berbers in the mountains north of Fez in Morocco, and experience the full extent of Spanish and Moorish influences on Moroccan cuisine in Tetouan - the gastro and poultry capital of the country. The boys also make their own rose and pistachio ice cream to cool down after a visit to a Hamman and are taught how to make a special pastry for their piece de resistance - chicken pastilla pie

programme.title: Indian Ocean with Simon Reeve
programme.desc: Adventurer Simon Reeve sets out to travel around the coastline of the Indian Ocean, journeying by boat, car, train and plane as he takes in 16 countries. He starts on the tip of South Africa, where he dives with ragged-tooth sharks and joins conservationists helping to save the endangered African penguin, before heading into Cape Town, where he has a close encounter with a drug dealer. Moving on, he hitches a boat to Mozambique, where a nervous captain reveals the threat posed by Somali pirates, and completes this leg of his journey in Zanzibar, a tropical island steeped in the long history of the slave trade

programme.title: Indian Ocean with Simon Reeve
programme.desc: The adventurer's epic journey continues on the coast of Madagascar, where he goes spearfishing with the Vezo people, whose lifestyle is under threat from their own rapid population growth. On Mauritius, he visits slums that show a different side to the tourist paradise, and he ends this leg in the Seychelles, meeting an Englishman who is turning his private island into the world's smallest national park. Simon also joins the Dutch Special Forces, training to board pirate ships operating on the high seas

programme.title: Indian Ocean with Simon Reeve
programme.desc: The third leg of the adventurer's journey takes him from the south of Kenya to the Horn of Africa. Along the way he joins a Ugandan peace-keeping force in Mogadishu, the capital of war-torn Somalia, which turns out to be the most dangerous leg of his journey as he ends up under fire on the front line. In contrast, he finds neighbouring Somaliland a stable and democratic home to thousands of Somalis fleeing fighting and famine. In Kenya's Tana Delta, he meets villagers facing eviction from an area that the government is turning over to sugar cane production for bio-fuels

programme.title: Indian Ocean with Simon Reeve
programme.desc: The fourth leg of the adventurer's journey takes him from Oman to the Maldives. He starts in the Strait of Hormuz, where oil from the Gulf is shipped through the narrow channel, then moves on to Mumbai, the ocean's biggest port. In the Maldives, Simon finds arguably the most beautiful collection of tropical coral islands in the world - but the fragile underwater environment is a barometer for the changing nature of the sea, as he witnesses how bleaching has damaged the coral and an entire island has been manufactured as a landfill dump to deal with the problem of rubbish

programme.title: Villages by the Sea

programme.title: Indian Ocean with Simon Reeve
programme.desc: Adventurer Simon Reeve sets out to travel around the coastline of the Indian Ocean, journeying by boat, car, train and plane as he takes in 16 countries. He starts on the tip of South Africa, where he dives with ragged-tooth sharks and joins conservationists helping to save the endangered African penguin, before heading into Cape Town, where he has a close encounter with a drug dealer. Moving on, he hitches a boat to Mozambique, where a nervous captain reveals the threat posed by Somali pirates, and completes this leg of his journey in Zanzibar, a tropical island steeped in the long history of the slave trade

programme.title: Indian Ocean with Simon Reeve
programme.desc: The adventurer's epic journey continues on the coast of Madagascar, where he goes spearfishing with the Vezo people, whose lifestyle is under threat from their own rapid population growth. On Mauritius, he visits slums that show a different side to the tourist paradise, and he ends this leg in the Seychelles, meeting an Englishman who is turning his private island into the world's smallest national park. Simon also joins the Dutch Special Forces, training to board pirate ships operating on the high seas

programme.title: Indian Ocean with Simon Reeve
programme.desc: The third leg of the adventurer's journey takes him from the south of Kenya to the Horn of Africa. Along the way he joins a Ugandan peace-keeping force in Mogadishu, the capital of war-torn Somalia, which turns out to be the most dangerous leg of his journey as he ends up under fire on the front line. In contrast, he finds neighbouring Somaliland a stable and democratic home to thousands of Somalis fleeing fighting and famine. In Kenya's Tana Delta, he meets villagers facing eviction from an area that the government is turning over to sugar cane production for bio-fuels

programme.title: Indian Ocean with Simon Reeve
programme.desc: The fourth leg of the adventurer's journey takes him from Oman to the Maldives. He starts in the Strait of Hormuz, where oil from the Gulf is shipped through the narrow channel, then moves on to Mumbai, the ocean's biggest port. In the Maldives, Simon finds arguably the most beautiful collection of tropical coral islands in the world - but the fragile underwater environment is a barometer for the changing nature of the sea, as he witnesses how bleaching has damaged the coral and an entire island has been manufactured as a landfill dump to deal with the problem of rubbish
